MALCOLM, 2026-08-25: 'you are using the matrixyl color scheme for the diagram. but please use generic skin colors here. see also this example: skingenetix-cpr-r3-set-nbp_flash_01.png'.

HE IS RIGHT, AND ROUND 1 APPLIED A RULE THAT DOES NOT REACH THIS SLOT. The concern-to-colour map in 03-art-direction-and-briefs.md §1.2 binds Firming & Skin Density to Matrixyl 3000's Teal 016569, and round 1 read that as 'the fibres are teal'. But that map exists to colour the CONCERN TILES and banners — the furniture that has to be told apart at a glance across a grid. An anatomy diagram is not furniture. On the reference Malcolm named, the r3 set as it reads on the page, the tissue is warm cream and blush throughout and the ONLY saturated colour in the frame is the ingredient itself: copper beads in f1 and f2, blue fibres in f1 where blue IS that page's active. Here there is no active in the frame at all, because this block is the damage, before any product is mentioned. So there is nothing for a brand colour to belong to, and a teal dermis just makes the anatomy look dyed.

PALETTE, ROUND 2 — SKIN AND NOTHING ELSE:
  tissue ground   soft desaturated peach-cream, warm, pale, matte (unchanged from r3)
  outer layer     the same cream, finely tiled
  cell rows       pale peach, rounded, translucent
  fibre bundles   PALE PEARL IVORY, almost white, the faintest warm gold only in the highlights
  fat lobules     pale warm cream
  ground          the r3 background: a very pale cool grey-white haze

THE FIBRES ARE SEPARATED BY MATERIAL, NOT BY HUE, and this is the whole risk of the round. Round 1 could rely on teal to make the collagen legible against peach. Take the hue away and cream fibre in a cream ground can vanish. So every brief now states the separation explicitly in the terms that actually carry it: the fibres are GLOSSY, TRANSLUCENT, SHARPLY DEFINED and LIGHTER IN VALUE, lying in a ground that is MATTE, OPAQUE, SOFTER and slightly deeper and warmer. That is also how real anatomical CGI reads collagen, and how real collagen looks — it is white, not teal.

AND IT GIVES THE DAMAGE A BETTER SIGNAL. In round 1 a degraded fibre had to be shown as 'greyed teal', which is a colour nobody can name. In a skin palette, a fibre that has been broken down LOSES ITS LUSTRE: pearl ivory going dull, chalky and greyed-beige, glassy going matte. Loss of gloss reads instantly and needs no key.

TEAL AND EVERY OTHER BRAND COLOUR ARE NOW NEGATED BY NAME — teal, blue-green, clinical blue, cobalt, copper, gold, green, purple — so no supplier reintroduces the r1 scheme from the family style it has been shown.

EVERYTHING ELSE IS UNCHANGED FROM ROUND 1, and is restated here so this file stands alone:

STYLE: the r3 / matrixyl house register — smooth glossy CGI, luminous and dreamy, high-key on a pale hazy gradient ground, a layered cross-section with legible strata, soft diffuse light, no hard shadow, shallow depth of field. No lettering of any kind, no arrows, no callouts, no infographic furniture. Square 2048x2048: the row height in `media-with-text` is set by the master's own aspect, so anything other than 1:1 makes this block taller than the other five.

IT IS A PICTURE OF LOSS, WHICH IS WHY THE FAMILY'S OWN DEVICES ARE NEGATED. Every explainer chosen on this store so far shows an active arriving and a structure being built — spheres above the surface, shafts of light descending, glints at the point of arrival, new fibre streaming from a cell. Malcolm's reference has all of those. This block makes the opposite claim, and the very next block on the page ('The Collagen-Peptide Approach to Firming') is where the repair belongs. If this frame carries spheres, shafts, chains or glints it will read as the treatment working and the page will argue backwards. So they stay negated by name — the one thing deliberately NOT taken from the named reference, and the one call to overrule if the intent was to match it device for device.

WHAT THE COPY CLAIMS, and which concept carries which:
  1. Collagen degradation — MMPs break collagen down faster than it is replaced. Carried by A as notched, eroded, fraying bundles, and by C as a density falloff.
  2. Elastin fragmentation — barely replaced after adolescence; once damaged the fibres fragment and cannot reassemble, so the loss is permanent. Carried by B, the only concept showing snapped, recoiled ends.
  3. Fat pad redistribution — the deep fat pads shrink and slide downward. Carried by C, the only concept deep enough to include that stratum.
  4. Hormonal change — a driver, not a visible structure. Not depicted, and nothing should try to.

NO MMP IS DRAWN AS A CHARACTER. An enzyme rendered as an agent chewing a fibre comes back as bacteria or an insect in every engine, and the copy asserts no such actor. Degradation is shown as its evidence — notched, thinned, fraying, parted fibre with fine drifting debris. Bacteria, viruses, insects, mites and worms are negated.

NO BEFORE-AND-AFTER SPLIT, on the r3 rule: a split frame asserts by juxtaposition and these engines render it as a hard seam. Contrast is a SMOOTH GRADIENT ACROSS ONE CONTINUOUS SCENE.

CLASS B THROUGHOUT — no product in frame, no references attached, no product description and no brand identity given to any engine. FLUX.2 is in the run: nothing for it to invent, and it is strong on abstract structural CGI — but check it at full size for printed numbers, which is a fixed trait. On round 1 it also blew the block apart into flying debris on slot A; if it does that again it is simply out for this brief.

JUDGE AT 100% AND AGAIN AT RENDER SIZE. The failure mode is TEXTURE COHERENCE, not lettering: bundles that resolve into textile, rope, web, knitting or twigs instead of collagen. Round 1's seedream slot-A candidates failed exactly this way — chunky broken sticks with debris that read as chipped shell, invisible on the contact sheet and obvious at native pixels. Those terms are negated, and the check is mandatory before anything is published.

slots.title: A · cross-section, the dermal scaffold thinned and parted, the surface sinking into it
slots.prompt:
Soft three-dimensional medical explainer illustration in the style of premium skincare advertising: smooth glossy CGI, luminous and dreamy, high-key on a pale hazy gradient background. Square format.

A small block of skin is shown in cross-section from a low three-quarter angle, isolated in clean empty space with nothing around it, floating on a smooth translucent base. Three strata are legible. Across the top, a thin outer layer with a fine irregular texture of soft interlocking plates. Beneath it, a stack of two or three rows of flattened rounded translucent cells packed neatly together. Below that, filling most of the block, an open zone of long wavy bundles of fibre running horizontally, curving and overlapping in loose parallel waves.

THE WHOLE PICTURE IS SKIN-COLOURED. The tissue is a soft desaturated peach-cream, warm, pale and matte. The fibre bundles are a pale pearl ivory, almost white, with only the faintest warm gold in their highlights. They are told apart from the tissue around them by MATERIAL AND NOT BY COLOUR: the bundles are glossy, translucent, crisply defined and lighter in value, catching a clean highlight along their length, while the ground they lie in is matte, opaque, softer-edged and very slightly deeper and warmer. Nothing in the frame is dyed or tinted.

THE SCAFFOLD HAS BEEN LOST, AND THE SURFACE IS FOLLOWING IT DOWN. The bundles are thin, slack and unevenly spaced, with wide empty gaps opened between them where a dense weave used to be. Many are notched and eroded along their length, worn narrow in the middle like a frayed cord. Where a bundle has been damaged IT LOSES ITS LUSTRE: the pearl ivory goes dull, chalky and greyed-beige and the glassy surface turns matte, so the worn fibre is unmistakably a different material from the bright intact fibre beside it. Several bundles have parted entirely and the two ends have drawn back from each other and curled, leaving a clear gap of empty space between them; the ends are blunt and slightly swollen and do not meet. A fine drift of tiny pale fragments hangs in the open space around the worst-damaged bundles.

Because the scaffold beneath it has thinned, the outer layer sags: it is drawn down into one long soft valley across the middle of the block, thinner and stretched where it dips, the cell rows compressed under the dip. Toward one end of the block the fibres are a little denser and brighter and the surface there is still level, and the change between the two is a slow smooth gradient across one continuous surface, never a line or an edge.

Nothing is arriving, nothing is being rebuilt, and the block is empty of anything but tissue. Soft diffuse light, no hard shadow, shallow depth of field, the far edge of the block dissolving into pale haze. Glossy, luminous, immaculate.

slots.title: B · macro of the elastic network, fibres snapped mid-span with the ends recoiled
slots.prompt:
Soft three-dimensional medical explainer illustration in the style of premium skincare advertising: smooth glossy CGI, luminous and dreamy, high-key on a pale hazy gradient background. Square format.

An extreme macro view deep inside a mesh of long elastic fibres, filling the frame edge to edge with no container and no surrounding scene, as though the camera is inside the material itself. The strands are smooth, glossy and translucent, each with a fine natural spring to it, crossing and interlacing at shallow angles and running away into a soft out-of-focus haze at the back of the frame.

THE WHOLE PICTURE IS SKIN-COLOURED. The strands are a pale pearl ivory, almost white, with only the faintest warm gold in their highlights, and the haze behind them is a soft warm peach-cream deepening gently toward the corners. The strands read as a different material from their surroundings because they are glassy, translucent and crisply lit against a soft matte ground, not because they are a different colour. Nothing in the frame is dyed or tinted.

THE MESH HAS BROKEN AND IT CANNOT COME BACK TOGETHER. Through the middle of the frame many strands have snapped part way along their span. At every break the two ends have sprung apart and recoiled into loose spirals — springs released and left slack — and the parted ends now hang a clear distance from one another with soft empty space between. The ends are blunt and slightly bulbous, torn rather than cut. Where a strand has broken IT LOSES ITS LUSTRE: the pearl ivory dulls to a chalky greyed beige and the glassy surface goes matte, so the damaged strands are plainly a duller material than the bright ones. Short orphaned pieces drift free in the gaps, curled and going nowhere, and a fine dust of pale fragments hangs in the light.

Where the strands are still whole they are taut, springy, brilliantly pearlescent and evenly spaced, carrying a clean highlight along their length. This intact region sits toward one corner of the frame and gives way to the broken region through a slow smooth gradient — density, brightness and gloss falling away gradually across one continuous mesh, with no line, no edge and no seam anywhere in the picture.

The mesh sags in the broken region, hanging heavier and lower than the taut corner, so the material visibly loses its spring across the frame. Nothing is arriving, nothing is being rebuilt. Shallow depth of field, soft diffuse light, no hard shadow. Glossy, luminous, immaculate.

slots.title: C · full-depth block, dense matrix falling away to sparse with the fat layer thinned and slipped
slots.prompt:
Soft three-dimensional medical explainer illustration in the style of premium skincare advertising: smooth glossy CGI, luminous and dreamy, high-key on a pale hazy gradient background. Square format.

A long low block of skin is shown in cross-section from a low three-quarter angle, isolated in clean empty space with nothing around it and floating on a smooth translucent base, so it reads as a specimen rather than part of a body. It is seen from the side so its full depth is legible, four strata stacked from top to bottom: a thin outer layer with a fine irregular texture of soft interlocking plates; beneath it a band of small pale rounded cells packed in neat rows; below that the thickest layer, an open zone of long wavy fibre bundles lying in horizontal courses; and at the very bottom a deep cushion of large soft rounded translucent lobules clustered together like a bed of smooth pebbles.

THE WHOLE PICTURE IS SKIN-COLOURED. Tissue and lobules are a soft desaturated peach-cream, warm, pale and matte; the fibre bundles are a pale pearl ivory, almost white, with only the faintest warm gold in their highlights. The bundles stand out because they are glossy, translucent, crisply defined and lighter in value against a matte, opaque, slightly deeper and warmer ground — separated by material, never by hue. Nothing in the frame is dyed or tinted.

EVERYTHING THINS FROM ONE END OF THE BLOCK TO THE OTHER, SMOOTHLY AND CONTINUOUSLY. At the left end the fibre zone is dense, thick, evenly woven and brightly pearlescent, the cushion of lobules beneath it is deep and full and round, and the outer surface above is level and taut. Travelling toward the right end, the bundles gradually become fewer, thinner and duller — the pearl lustre going chalky and greyed-beige, glassy turning matte — worn narrow and frayed in places and parted in others with the ends drawn back and curled; the gaps between them widen until they are mostly empty space; the cushion of lobules loses depth, its lobules shrinking and flattening and sliding downward and to the right so the bed of them slumps away from the layers above and leaves a soft hollow beneath them; and the outer surface, unsupported, sinks into a long slack downward curve and gathers into a soft fold near the right end where it has more area than it has structure to hold.

The change from one end to the other is a slow even gradient across one continuous block — no line, no seam, no join, no division, nothing repeated and nothing mirrored. A fine drift of tiny pale fragments hangs in the open gaps at the sparse end.

Nothing is arriving and nothing is being rebuilt. Soft diffuse light, no hard shadow, shallow depth of field, the far edge of the block dissolving into pale haze. Glossy, luminous, immaculate.
